text.p: Workers at the Jamaica Grande resort in Ocho Rios will return to work Friday, ending a five-day strike that virtually shut down the Renaissance Hotel Group NV-managed hotel, a union said Thursday.
The 700 workers will return to their jobs because the hotel had agreed to turn over a list of employees for a poll on unionization, the National Workers Union said.

The 725-room resort reported 80 percent to 85 percent occupancy when the strike began. The hotel is now virtually deserted as a result of the strike. Hotel officials put the losses at between $4 million and $5 million.
The workers struck after four years of unsuccessful efforts by the National Workers Union to hold a vote on whether hotel employees wanted union representation.
Two years ago, the government's industrial disputes tribunal ordered the hotel to provide a list of employees for the poll.
The hotel maintains that certain categories of workers should be excluded from unionization.
The Jamaican government owns 49 percent of the hotel, which it acquired after it took over the failed Century National Bank more than a year ago.
